unguided Internet CCBT I for insomnia has sustained effects on insomnia symptoms and daytime functioning up to 18 month after the intervention period.

this study shows that unguided Internet delivered cognitive behavioral treatment for insomnia has a sustained positive effect on sleep, daytime fatigue, psychological distress and beliefs about sleep at least 18 months after intervention.
unguided Internet based cognitive behavioral therapy for chronic insomnia appears to have sustained positive effects on sleep, fatigue, and beliefs about insomnia up to 18 month posttreatment.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed an unguided Internet based cognitive behavioral therapy for chronic insomnia that has been tested on a large scale in a randomized controlled design and that has shown long term effects on insomnia and related daytime symptoms.
the Internet delivered CBT-I was effective in reducing insomnia and improving daytime functioning in the short-term and in the long-term.
the Internet based treatment is an effective treatment for insomnia and has good long term results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
unguided Internet CCBT I has sustained positive effects on sleep, fatigue, distress, and beliefs about insomnia 18 months after treatment.
unguided internet CBT-I appears to have sustained long term effects on sleep, sleep related daytime functioning, and sleep related cognitions.
Internet delivered cognitive behavioral treatment for insomnia is effective in the long term, and that the effects are not only maintained, but also seem to be enhanced over time.
